 Local singer Lillie Kolich advances on ‘The Voice’
 Albuquerque singer Lillie Kolich advanced to cut week on "The Voice" after winning her battle round with a performance coaches praised as uniquely her own. ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. – Albuquerque singer Lillie Kolich advanced to cut week on “The Voice” after winning her battle round with a performance coaches praised as uniquely her own.
 KOB 4 reporter Alika Medina spoke with Kolich this week after the performance, which moved her on after the battle rounds.
 Kolich faced Kayleigh Mathews in this week’s battle round of “The Voice” as they sang “Girl Crush” by Little Big Town.
 “You know it’s funny. I live in Nashville and I write country songs for other artists, but like country music is not my bag,” Kolich said.
 “I knew that she was gonna take the very like classic country approach,” Kolich said. “So I was like, I have to kind of keep this in my world and in my lane because if I try to meet her where she’s at, it’s just not going to work for me.”
 Kolich said the choice felt risky as she tried to put her own stamp on the song and stay in her lane.
 “I was actually just like very surprised in general when I won.” Kolich said.
 Queen Latifah chose Kolich in the battle round.
 “I picked Lillie because she has a flavor that is all on her own,” Queen Latifah said. “She sang one note today that was so special and unique, I said I got to choose her.”
 Kolich said one note in the performance became a turning point after others in rehearsal had encouraged her not to do it.
 “Like everyone when we were rehearsing was like encouraging me to like not do that. So that was very reassuring because she was like, ‘This is kind of like that choice was just like so special and like proved like your uniqueness,'” Kolich said.
 Kolich said she will sing an unusual choice next as she heads into cut week, which is set to air Nov. 2.
 “I’m singing a very very interesting song. It’s actually one of my favorite songs ever, but it’s very like out of my lane, and I’m reworking it to make it like a Lillie song,” Kolich said.
